 Flood Warning is in effect ASU kickoff pushed back after FAA ground stop disrupts team’s travel to Florida 
 Sun Devils will attempt to fly to Orlando on Saturday 
 A nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration disrupted travel for the Arizona State football team Friday, delaying its trip to Florida By Ben Bradley Published : Nov. 13, 2026 at 4:58 PM MST | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily) — A nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration disrupted travel for the Arizona State football team Friday, delaying its trip to Florida for Saturday’s game against the University of Central Florida.
 Kickoff in Orlando has been moved back two hours to 3:30 p.m. Mountain time, or 5:30 p.m. Eastern time. The FAA has since lifted the ground stop.
 View this post on Instagram 
 The Sun Devils were scheduled to depart Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport on Friday afternoon. But after the ground stop passed the two-hour mark, the team returned to Tempe and planned to fly out Saturday morning.
 The disruption also affected college football teams around the country. ESPN reported that travel for at least 10 Power Four conference teams was affected.
 Utah, which is scheduled to play the Arizona Wildcats in Tucson, was unable to depart. That game has been delayed three hours to 8:30 p.m. 
 Flights were halted shortly after 2 p.m. because of air traffic control communications problems, according to the FAA.
 Statement from the Big 12 Conference on FAA Ground Stop pic.twitter.com/OQP0d46c1N
